installLicensePanel.heading: Four steps. Your prompts never touch our servers.
installLicensePanel.step1: 1 · Get your license key — the SDK is public but fail-closed; it only runs with a valid key. Passed as licenseKey.
installLicensePanel.step2: 2 · Create & verify a service-account key — a machine credential (bvk_…) that does two jobs: it reports counts-only usage (your seats & savings), and it lets the SDK collect your renewed license by itself every billing period. Separate from the license key; only its hash is stored. Create one, then Test my key to confirm it's live.
installLicensePanel.shownOnce: shown once at creation — only the prefix is stored.
installLicensePanel.renewalNote: Keep this key in your deployment. Your license expires at the end of each billing period and the renewal mints a new one. With this key the SDK collects it and swaps it in without a restart. Without it nobody collects it, so someone has to paste the new key by hand every period — and if nobody does, the SDK stops once the grace period ends, even though the subscription is paid and up to date.
installLicensePanel.step3: 3 · Install — public on npm, no token, no config.
installLicensePanel.step4: 4 · Wire your provider & read the SavingsReport
installLicensePanel.gatewayNote: Coding terminal instead of an app? The same package ships a local measuring gateway: bvsala claude launches Claude Code through it and this dashboard shows the spend, token by token. Also bvsala codex, bvsala goose and bvsala qwen; bvsala doctor prints the exact block for the rest. It uses the same service key from step 2 — measuring needs no license key.
installLicensePanel.finalNote: That's it. No valid license → generate() refuses. If your plan is cancelled the SDK stops within ~15 min via licenseServerUrl — no restart, and it never bricks your production if we're unreachable.

cascade.title: Cheapest execution wins

steps.title: Compress what remains
steps.sub: leaner encoding · only when it pays off

cascade.footnote: Each step falls into ONE different ledger, so these figures do not add up to each other. A step whose ledger does not clear zero does not appear here: output restriction was measured and does not save, so it is not advertised. Every figure in this run is from gpt-4o-mini: the same lever can cost money on another model, and that is published too.

explica.title: What does Savings actually do?
explica.sub: Four ideas, four eight-second animations. That's the whole product.

pasos.title: AI charges you per word
pasos.body: Every request to an AI is paid for by the text going in and out. Savings stands in the middle of that path and lets through only what's needed: whatever you didn't have to pay for drops into your jar.

pasos.title: You don't pay twice for the same thing
pasos.body: An AI re-reads everything you already sent it, turn after turn — and the provider charges for it again. Savings prepares every request so the provider applies its discounted price to the repeats. The discount is the provider's; our part is asking for it properly.

pasos.title: A receipt you can verify
pasos.body: We don't ask for faith. Every saving is measured with the provider's official meter — the same one they bill you with — and lands on your receipt. Anything that can't be checked against the bill is never announced.

pasos.title: We only earn when you save
pasos.body: Our commission comes out of the measured saving, never out of your pocket: most of what you save always stays with you. A month with no savings? Zero commission.

explica.nota: The animations illustrate the idea. The real numbers — measured against live providers — are right below.

step2.title: How do we know it saves? We measure it — and we publish every trial, one by one.
step2.body: Every scenario runs twice against the real provider: as-is, and with Savings in front. Both results are counted with the provider's own meter — the same one that prices your bill. Here is what came out, error margin included:
step2.videoCaption: The test is a fair experiment: the same task twice — without Savings and with Savings — with the provider's own meter counting both.
step2.plain: In this test, the bill went down by at least {piso}, with near certainty. Most likely it went down by {punto}.
step2.plainNote: When there's a range, we always announce the small number — the one statistics guarantees — never the flattering one.

ledgersHead.title: Every kind of saving, counted separately — so no number gets inflated.
ledgersHead.body: Savings saves in several ways: it avoids whole calls, removes text you didn't need, packs what's sent more tightly, and switches on the provider's discounts. Each way keeps its own ledger with its own measured figure — and we never add them up into one marketing number.
ledgersHead.providerNote: Each ledger is measured and published on its own against the OpenAI API; the ones that do not clear zero do not appear. A percentage without its model next to it means nothing: the same lever can save on one model and cost on another.

skill.title: The skill that stretches your subscription caps
skill.body: No invoice doesn't mean no pain: the five-hour window and the weekly cap. savings-mode is a pure-instructions skill — no proxy, your traffic untouched — that cuts the two masses that actually burn cap: model output and tool results. It's free; what you pay Savings for is knowing how much it saves you.
skill.mLecturaDesc: The whole context is re-read every turn — which is why keeping it lean matters.
skill.mEscrituraDesc: Every tool result is cache-written at a premium before being re-read.
skill.mSalidaDesc: Under one percent of the tokens; the skill attacks it directly.
skill.anatomiaNota: Measured with the meter over {peticiones} real Claude Code requests, against the provider's own counters ({fecha}). The skill's own effect will be published once A/B-measured — never before.
skill.ccNota: One command: installs into ~/.claude/skills and activates by itself when the conversation turns to limits or saving tokens.
skill.cxNota: Codex has no skills: the same discipline ships as a marked block in your AGENTS.md (~/.codex) — always on; delete the block to turn it off. Your AGENTS.md outside the marks is never touched. Works with ChatGPT accounts and API keys, and under bvsala codex its effect is measured.
skill.aiCuenta: The download asks for your (free) Savings account: adoption becomes a real metric, with identity — the skill itself carries no telemetry at all.
skill.aiPaso1: On claude.ai enable “Code execution and file creation” (Settings → Capabilities).
skill.aiPaso2: Then upload the zip under Customize → Skills: it appears with its own toggle, private to your account.

gateway.title: Claude Code on an API key? See its real spend, token by token.
gateway.body: One command puts a local meter in front of your terminal. No code changes, nothing to configure — and your prompts never leave your machine: only counts and cost reach this dashboard.
gateway.note: The gateway measures every request. With a PRO license it also applies one lever by default: it shortens the cache-write TTL while your session stays hot — that changes the price, never the content the model reads. The other levers stay off until you switch them on. The savings-mode skill is available for your caps, with its effect still to be measured. It also works with Codex CLI, Goose and Qwen Code — and bvsala doctor prints the exact configuration for the rest.

formula.title: How what you pay us is calculated
formula.mes1: Your first month: only {precioMes} per seat. We measure everything and charge no commission — at close you'll see the exact statement of what it would have cost.
formula.medido: After that, commission only on measured savings: the kind you can reconcile against your provider's invoice. Estimated savings are never billed.
formula.garantia: And you always keep {garantia} or more of every euro saved: the commission only exists when your measured savings exist.
formula.tramos: Tiered, each bracket at its own rate — {tramos}. The more you save, the lower our percentage.
formula.permanencia: A month with no savings? Commission: {cero}. No lock-in — and your first variable invoice only contains numbers you already saw on your statement.

devs.title: Fewer bill headaches. Without changing provider.
devs.sub: Three facts about the package. None of them is a promise.

cards.title: Zero runtime dependencies
cards.body: A single ESM bundle. Nothing gets installed next to your code that we did not write; the exact tokenizer is an optional peer.

cards.title: One SavingsReport per call
cards.body: Four ledgers that are never summed, the cost with its basis (measured or estimated) and traces per stage. It is the same thing your dashboard reads.

cards.title: Your traffic still goes direct
cards.body: The SDK wraps the call inside your process. Your prompts never pass through BiVelio: we only ever receive counts and cost.

howItWorks.metaTitle: Where does the saving install? · BiVelio Savings Layer
howItWorks.metaDescription: BV‑SALA is a layer that installs in your application's code, where the API is called. What it can save, where it doesn't apply, and how it's truly measured.
howItWorks.title: Where does the saving install?
howItWorks.lede: BV‑SALA is not an app, not an extension, not a ChatGPT setting. It's a piece of code a developer places inside their own application, right where that application calls your provider's API. It can only save where a per-token bill exists — and can only measure it where it sees every request go by.
howItWorks.s1Title: The layer lives inside your code
howItWorks.s1Sub: The same call, with and without the layer. Traffic always travels straight from your application to the provider — BV‑SALA is not a middleman server and never sees your data from outside.
howItWorks.s1Note: That green box is an npm package inside the application's code. That's why the key question is never “what do I install?” but “who wrote the code that calls the API?” — that person is who can install it. The one exception is a coding terminal like Claude Code: there the “bvsala claude” gateway sits in front without touching a single line of code.
howItWorks.s2Sub: Four ways of using AI, and what BV‑SALA can do in each one.
howItWorks.caseChatSub: app or web, free or paid
howItWorks.caseChatBody: You pay a flat fee (or nothing): there is no per-token bill to reduce, and it's a closed product where nobody can place software between the app and its models. BV‑SALA's saving simply doesn't apply here — and no product can honestly promise it there.
howItWorks.caseClaudeBody: Flat subscription: no token invoice to meter — but there are caps (the five-hour window and the weekly one). That is exactly what the savings-mode skill is for: free, uploaded to claude.ai in a minute, attacking the two masses that burn cap. Its effect will be published once measured — never before.
howItWorks.caseCodeBody: On a subscription the fee is flat — but capped: the same skill installs with a single command and stretches the same weekly cap. With an API key there is a real token invoice — and the meter is already running: “bvsala claude” launches Claude Code through the local gateway and your spend shows up in the panel, token by token, without touching a line of code. Savings there are the next phase — first we measure for real.
howItWorks.caseAppBody: The case BV‑SALA exists for. Your app calls the API with your key, the provider bills every token, and the layer installs in three steps: package, license, and wrapping the call. From the first request it returns a SavingsReport with the saving, split into measured and estimated.
howItWorks.s3Sub: The product has two different numbers, and they shouldn't be mixed.
howItWorks.mBeforeBody: The calculator in the pricing section projects your savings from your own numbers: requests, tokens and model. It's an honest projection — that's why it carries the “estimate” tag.
howItWorks.mAfterBody: Every call returns a SavingsReport: the calls you never paid for and the net saving per request. Auditable, request by request, on your own infrastructure.
